title: A guide welcomes, never gatekeeps
statement: Write a guide's lines as a welcome, never as a gatekeeper withholding answers, and fix a patronising guide by changing its stance toward the learner, not its words.
example: The rejected intro line was 'I won't hand you the answers. I'll make you earn them'; its replacement says readers have followed this story for four hundred years.
detail: Feedback on a Grade 9 unit film called its guide's intro, "I won't hand you the answers. I'll make you earn them", a young gatekeeper stance, and patronising. The voice direction was rewritten as an elder glad a new reader has come, warm and never patronising, the film's closing scene gained a line of welcome, and the design has the check-card copy follow the declarative feedback lines rather than the intro. This is one review's verdict; there are no learner data on how teenagers hear either stance.
against: The stance explanation is a review note, which the review says is rationale that has not been confirmed (`g9/sources/Othello_1_Feedback_DevFactory.md`, line 13), and the recast is still marked open in its checklist (line 69).

evidence.quote: The *intro* lines are the problem: "I won't hand you the answers. I'll make you earn them" is the young gatekeeper stance she calls patronising (4.2).
**the feedback lines are the best copy in the build** — declarative, one fact, no praise inflation, no exclamation marks, every wrong answer corrected with the reason.
Card copy should follow the feedback lines, not the intro.
Elder storyteller: wisdom of time and knowledge, glad a new reader has come; warm and grave, never patronizing; ominous only where the words turn dark.
Readers have followed this story for four hundred years. Now it is your turn.
Speak directly to one young reader who has just paused the film: melancholy and watchful, but not slow; short, clear sentences; a guide, not the show; warm but never patronizing.
At times the character feels patronizing again, and I don’t like that she’s young.
Register: the wisdom of time and knowledge, plus the excitement that a new reader has arrived.
The mechanism behind "patronizing" is stance rather than vocabulary.
A young guide explaining things to a child reads as condescension between peers; an elder sharing something they consider precious reads as initiation.
The same sentence can do either depending on who is saying it and why, so the fix is about the relationship the character is in, not about simplifying or complicating the words.
Anything under "Note" is an observation made during the review rather than part of that feedback — it is offered as rationale and has not been confirmed.
